claim: Myelinating oligodendrocytes are essential for central nervous system (CNS) formation and function.
source: Myelinating oligodendrocytes are essential for central nervous system (CNS) formation and function.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about oligodendrocyte function.

claim: Disruption of myelinating oligodendrocytes is implicated in numerous neurodevelopmental, neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders.
source: Their disruption is implicated in numerous neurodevelopmental, neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by established scientific consensus.

claim: Recent studies have indicated that oligodendrocytes may be tractable for treatment of disease.
source: However, recent studies have indicated that oligodendrocytes may be tractable for treatment of disease.
evidence: This statement references recent studies without specific citations in this sentence.

claim: Zebrafish have become well established for the study of myelinating oligodendrocyte biology and drug discovery in vivo in recent years.
source: In recent years, zebrafish have become well established for the study of myelinating oligodendrocyte biology and drug discovery in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the field's adoption of zebrafish as a model system.

claim: Automating the delivery of zebrafish larvae to a spinning disk confocal microscope enabled automated high-resolution imaging of myelinating oligodendrocytes in vivo.
source: Here, by automating the delivery of zebrafish larvae to a spinning disk confocal microscope, we were able to automate high-resolution imaging of myelinating oligodendrocytes in vivo.
evidence: This describes the technical achievement of the study.

claim: An image analysis pipeline was developed that facilitated a screen of compounds with epigenetic and post-translational targets for their effects on regulating myelinating oligodendrocyte number.
source: From there, we developed an image analysis pipeline that facilitated a screen of compounds with epigenetic and post-translational targets for their effects on regulating myelinating oligodendrocyte number.
evidence: This describes the methodology developed in the study.

claim: The screen identified novel compounds that strongly promote myelinating oligodendrocyte formation in vivo.
source: This screen identified novel compounds that strongly promote myelinating oligodendrocyte formation in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: The imaging platform and analysis pipeline is flexible and can be employed for high-resolution imaging-based screens of broad interest using zebrafish.
source: Our imaging platform and analysis pipeline is flexible and can be employed for high-resolution imaging-based screens of broad interest using zebrafish.
evidence: This is a claim about the broader applicability of the developed methods.

claim: Myelin facilitates the rapid propagation of nerve impulses.
source: Myelin is a lipid-rich structure made by specialised glial cells, oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system (CNS) and Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system (PNS), that facilitates the rapid propagation of nerve impulses and provides trophic and metabolic support to axons (Nave and Werner, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Nave and Werner, 2014.

claim: Myelin provides trophic and metabolic support to axons.
source: Myelin is a lipid-rich structure made by specialised glial cells, oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system (CNS) and Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system (PNS), that facilitates the rapid propagation of nerve impulses and provides trophic and metabolic support to axons (Nave and Werner, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Nave and Werner, 2014.

claim: In mammals, myelination in the CNS starts around birth and continues well into adult life.
source: In mammals, myelination in the CNS starts around birth and continues well into adult life (Yeung et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Yeung et al., 2014.

claim: New myelin is thought to be generated by a combination of the differentiation of new oligodendrocytes and remodelling of existing myelin.
source: New myelin is thought to be generated by a combination of the differentiation of new oligodendrocytes (Hill et al., 2018; Hughes et al., 2018; Young et al., 2013) and remodelling of existing myelin (Auer et al., 2018; Snaidero et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: New oligodendrocytes can be produced throughout life by tissue-resident oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs).
source: New oligodendrocytes can be produced throughout life by tissue-resident oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), which represent about 5% of CNS cells life-long (Dawson et al., 2003), and to a lesser extent by neural stem cell-derived OPCs (Samanta et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Dawson et al., 2003 and Samanta et al., 2015.

claim: OPCs represent about 5% of CNS cells life-long.
source: New oligodendrocytes can be produced throughout life by tissue-resident oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), which represent about 5% of CNS cells life-long (Dawson et al., 2003), and to a lesser extent by neural stem cell-derived OPCs (Samanta et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Dawson et al., 2003.

claim: There is increasing evidence that myelination is controlled by neuronal activity.
source: There is increasing evidence that myelination is controlled by neuronal activity, and that regulation of myelin is important for both nervous system health and functional plasticity (Almeida and Lyons, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Almeida and Lyons, 2017.

claim: Regulation of myelin is important for both nervous system health and functional plasticity.
source: There is increasing evidence that myelination is controlled by neuronal activity, and that regulation of myelin is important for both nervous system health and functional plasticity (Almeida and Lyons, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Almeida and Lyons, 2017.

claim: Loss of myelin in late adulthood correlates with age-related cognitive decline.
source: Indeed, loss of myelin in late adulthood correlates with age-related cognitive decline (Deary et al., 2006; Lu et al., 2013; Penke et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Deary et al., 2006; Lu et al., 2013; Penke et al., 2010.

claim: Disruption to myelin and myelinating glia contributes to neonatal hypoxia.
source: These include: neonatal hypoxia (Buser et al., 2012); childhood leukodystrophies (Boespflug-Tanguy et al., 2008); neurodevelopmental disorders including autism (Pacey et al., 2013) and schizophrenia (Hercher et al., 2014); as well as neurodegenerative conditions including multiple sclerosis (MS) (Compston and Coles, 2008), motor neuron disease (Kang et al., 2013), Huntington's disease (Huang et al., 2015) and Alzheimer's disease (Bartzokis, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Buser et al., 2012.

claim: Disruption to myelin and myelinating glia contributes to childhood leukodystrophies.
source: These include: neonatal hypoxia (Buser et al., 2012); childhood leukodystrophies (Boespflug-Tanguy et al., 2008); neurodevelopmental disorders including autism (Pacey et al., 2013) and schizophrenia (Hercher et al., 2014); as well as neurodegenerative conditions including multiple sclerosis (MS) (Compston and Coles, 2008), motor neuron disease (Kang et al., 2013), Huntington's disease (Huang et al., 2015) and Alzheimer's disease (Bartzokis, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Boespflug-Tanguy et al., 2008.

claim: Disruption to myelin and myelinating glia contributes to autism.
source: These include: neonatal hypoxia (Buser et al., 2012); childhood leukodystrophies (Boespflug-Tanguy et al., 2008); neurodevelopmental disorders including autism (Pacey et al., 2013) and schizophrenia (Hercher et al., 2014); as well as neurodegenerative conditions including multiple sclerosis (MS) (Compston and Coles, 2008), motor neuron disease (Kang et al., 2013), Huntington's disease (Huang et al., 2015) and Alzheimer's disease (Bartzokis, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pacey et al., 2013.

claim: Disruption to myelin and myelinating glia contributes to schizophrenia.
source: These include: neonatal hypoxia (Buser et al., 2012); childhood leukodystrophies (Boespflug-Tanguy et al., 2008); neurodevelopmental disorders including autism (Pacey et al., 2013) and schizophrenia (Hercher et al., 2014); as well as neurodegenerative conditions including multiple sclerosis (MS) (Compston and Coles, 2008), motor neuron disease (Kang et al., 2013), Huntington's disease (Huang et al., 2015) and Alzheimer's disease (Bartzokis, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hercher et al., 2014.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Compston and Coles, 2008.

claim: Disruption to myelin and myelinating glia contributes to motor neuron disease.
source: These include: neonatal hypoxia (Buser et al., 2012); childhood leukodystrophies (Boespflug-Tanguy et al., 2008); neurodevelopmental disorders including autism (Pacey et al., 2013) and schizophrenia (Hercher et al., 2014); as well as neurodegenerative conditions including multiple sclerosis (MS) (Compston and Coles, 2008), motor neuron disease (Kang et al., 2013), Huntington's disease (Huang et al., 2015) and Alzheimer's disease (Bartzokis, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kang et al., 2013.

claim: Disruption to myelin and myelinating glia contributes to Huntington's disease.
source: These include: neonatal hypoxia (Buser et al., 2012); childhood leukodystrophies (Boespflug-Tanguy et al., 2008); neurodevelopmental disorders including autism (Pacey et al., 2013) and schizophrenia (Hercher et al., 2014); as well as neurodegenerative conditions including multiple sclerosis (MS) (Compston and Coles, 2008), motor neuron disease (Kang et al., 2013), Huntington's disease (Huang et al., 2015) and Alzheimer's disease (Bartzokis, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2015.

claim: Disruption to myelin and myelinating glia contributes to Alzheimer's disease.
source: These include: neonatal hypoxia (Buser et al., 2012); childhood leukodystrophies (Boespflug-Tanguy et al., 2008); neurodevelopmental disorders including autism (Pacey et al., 2013) and schizophrenia (Hercher et al., 2014); as well as neurodegenerative conditions including multiple sclerosis (MS) (Compston and Coles, 2008), motor neuron disease (Kang et al., 2013), Huntington's disease (Huang et al., 2015) and Alzheimer's disease (Bartzokis, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Bartzokis, 2011.

claim: Disruption to oligodendrocytes and myelin play important roles in the pathogenesis of glioma.
source: Furthermore, disruption to oligodendrocytes and myelin play important roles in the pathogenesis of glioma (Venkatesh et al., 2015) and white-matter stroke (Matute et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Venkatesh et al., 2015.

claim: Disruption to oligodendrocytes and myelin play important roles in the pathogenesis of white-matter stroke.
source: Furthermore, disruption to oligodendrocytes and myelin play important roles in the pathogenesis of glioma (Venkatesh et al., 2015) and white-matter stroke (Matute et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Matute et al., 2013.

claim: OPCs and neural stem cells present in the CNS throughout life can generate new oligodendrocytes following damage to myelin.
source: However, it is now clear that OPCs and neural stem cells present in the CNS throughout life can generate new oligodendrocytes following damage to myelin, and that these cells can in turn regenerate myelin through the process of remyelination (Franklin and ffrench-Constant, 2017; Prineas and Connell, 1979; Samanta et al., 2015; Zawadzka et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: New oligodendrocytes generated following myelin damage can regenerate myelin through the process of remyelination.
source: However, it is now clear that OPCs and neural stem cells present in the CNS throughout life can generate new oligodendrocytes following damage to myelin, and that these cells can in turn regenerate myelin through the process of remyelination (Franklin and ffrench-Constant, 2017; Prineas and Connell, 1979; Samanta et al., 2015; Zawadzka et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The capacity to generate myelin throughout life raises hope that the oligodendrocyte lineage may be tractable for the treatment of disease.
source: This capacity to generate myelin throughout life, including in response to damage, raises hope that the oligodendrocyte lineage may be tractable for the treatment of disease.
evidence: This is an inference based on the regenerative capacity of oligodendrocytes.

claim: Multiple bottlenecks can limit the normal formation or regeneration of myelinating oligodendrocytes, including disruption to OPC specification, proliferation, migration, oligodendrocyte differentiation or (re)myelination.
source: Depending on the specific disease, multiple bottlenecks can limit the normal formation or regeneration of myelinating oligodendrocytes, including disruption to OPC specification, proliferation, migration, oligodendrocyte differentiation or (re)myelination, reviewed by (Cole et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cole et al., 2017.

claim: In MS, certain areas with demyelinated axons completely lack OPCs.
source: For example, in MS, while certain areas with demyelinated axons completely lack OPCs, others have plentiful OPCs that do not differentiate into oligodendrocytes (Boyd et al., 2013; Chang et al., 2000; Kuhlmann et al., 2008; Lucchinetti et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In MS, some areas have plentiful OPCs that do not differentiate into oligodendrocytes.
source: For example, in MS, while certain areas with demyelinated axons completely lack OPCs, others have plentiful OPCs that do not differentiate into oligodendrocytes (Boyd et al., 2013; Chang et al., 2000; Kuhlmann et al., 2008; Lucchinetti et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: When oligodendrocytes differentiate and regenerate myelin, new myelin sheaths are characterised by being shorter and thinner than normal.
source: Even when oligodendrocytes differentiate and regenerate myelin, new myelin sheaths are characterised by being shorter and thinner than normal (Franklin and ffrench-Constant, 2017; Prineas and Connell, 1979).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Franklin and ffrench-Constant, 2017; Prineas and Connell, 1979.

claim: Recent unbiased phenotypic screens have led to the identification of several hit compounds that promote oligodendrocyte differentiation in vitro.
source: Indeed, recent unbiased phenotypic screens have led to the identification of several hit compounds that promote oligodendrocyte differentiation in vitro (Deshmukh et al., 2013; Joubert et al., 2010; Mei et al., 2014; Mei et al., 2016; Najm et al., 2015; Peppard et al., 2015; Porcu et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: A number of hit compounds that promote oligodendrocyte differentiation in vitro have been validated in vivo.
source: A number of these hits have been validated in vivo (Cole et al., 2017), and one, clemastine, has even shown efficacy in improving optic nerve function in patients with MS (Green et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cole et al., 2017.

claim: Clemastine has shown efficacy in improving optic nerve function in patients with MS.
source: A number of these hits have been validated in vivo (Cole et al., 2017), and one, clemastine, has even shown efficacy in improving optic nerve function in patients with MS (Green et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Green et al., 2017.

claim: Phenotypic gene discovery screens have identified novel factors required for myelination.
source: Phenotypic gene discovery screens have identified novel factors required for myelination (for example Kearns et al., 2015; Lyons et al., 2009), and live imaging based studies have provided insight into cellular mechanisms of oligodendrocyte development and myelination (for example Almeida et al., 2011; Auer et al., 2018; Czopka et al., 2013; Kirby et al., 2006; Snaidero et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Kearns et al., 2015; Lyons et al., 2009.

claim: Live imaging based studies have provided insight into cellular mechanisms of oligodendrocyte development and myelination.
source: Phenotypic gene discovery screens have identified novel factors required for myelination (for example Kearns et al., 2015; Lyons et al., 2009), and live imaging based studies have provided insight into cellular mechanisms of oligodendrocyte development and myelination (for example Almeida et al., 2011; Auer et al., 2018; Czopka et al., 2013; Kirby et al., 2006; Snaidero et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Zebrafish embryos can be generated in very large numbers.
source: Zebrafish embryos can be generated in very large numbers and their externally fertilised eggs develop rapidly from a single cell to a freely swimming, optically transparent animal with extensive myelination in just a few days, meaning entire developmental events and biological processes can be observed in real time (for example Keller et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of zebrafish as a model organism.

claim: Zebrafish externally fertilised eggs develop rapidly from a single cell to a freely swimming, optically transparent animal with extensive myelination in just a few days.
source: Zebrafish embryos can be generated in very large numbers and their externally fertilised eggs develop rapidly from a single cell to a freely swimming, optically transparent animal with extensive myelination in just a few days, meaning entire developmental events and biological processes can be observed in real time (for example Keller et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about the developmental properties of zebrafish.

claim: Compounds can be taken up by zebrafish embryos following direct addition to the water.
source: Compounds can be taken up by the embryo following direct addition to the water, and phenotypic screens can be carried out either by direct assessment of organ formation, cardiovascular function, general development or behaviour, or using a variety of cell-type and tissue specific markers and reporters (for example Milan et al., 2003; North et al., 2007; Peterson et al., 2000, 2004; Rihel et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of zebrafish for drug screening.

claim: The first ground-breaking phenotypic chemical screen using zebrafish was in 2000.
source: Since the first ground-breaking phenotypic chemical screen using zebrafish in 2000 (Peterson et al., 2000), numerous others have followed (Rennekamp and Peterson, 2015), including assessment of oligodendrocyte lineage formation (Buckley et al., 2010) and a number that have led to new clinical trials (MacRae and Peterson, 2015; North et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Peterson et al., 2000.

claim: Some zebrafish chemical screens have led to new clinical trials.
source: Since the first ground-breaking phenotypic chemical screen using zebrafish in 2000 (Peterson et al., 2000), numerous others have followed (Rennekamp and Peterson, 2015), including assessment of oligodendrocyte lineage formation (Buckley et al., 2010) and a number that have led to new clinical trials (MacRae and Peterson, 2015; North et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to MacRae and Peterson, 2015; North et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2008.

claim: Using an in vivo system is particularly advantageous for screening complex biological processes, such as myelination, that are difficult to fully recapitulate in vitro.
source: Using an in vivo system is particularly advantageous for screening complex biological processes, such as myelination, that are difficult to fully recapitulate in vitro (Buckley et al., 2008), and recent advances in automated embryo handling technologies have made scalable in vivo screens using zebrafish feasible (Chang et al., 2012; Pardo-Martin et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Buckley et al., 2008.

claim: Recent advances in automated embryo handling technologies have made scalable in vivo screens using zebrafish feasible.
source: Using an in vivo system is particularly advantageous for screening complex biological processes, such as myelination, that are difficult to fully recapitulate in vitro (Buckley et al., 2008), and recent advances in automated embryo handling technologies have made scalable in vivo screens using zebrafish feasible (Chang et al., 2012; Pardo-Martin et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Chang et al., 2012; Pardo-Martin et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2015.

claim: The study combined a commercially available platform that automates the delivery of zebrafish from multi-well plates to a microscope platform with a customised spinning disk confocal microscope to automate high-resolution image acquisition.
source: Here we combine a commercially available platform that automates the delivery of zebrafish from multi-well plates to a microscope platform, with a customised spinning disk confocal microscope to automate high-resolution image acquisition.
evidence: This describes the technical setup of the study.

claim: The study developed an image handling and analysis pipeline that allowed execution of an automated screen which identified several novel hit compounds that regulate myelinating oligodendrocyte number.
source: We develop an image handling and analysis pipeline that allowed us to execute an automated screen which identified several novel hit compounds that regulate myelinating oligodendrocyte number.
evidence: This describes the primary findings of the study.

claim: The imaging and analysis capacities are expected to be broadly useful to researchers interested in executing scalable, high-resolution in vivo analyses of diverse biological processes in zebrafish.
source: In addition, we expect our imaging and analysis capacities to be broadly useful to researchers interested in executing scalable, high-resolution in vivo analyses of diverse biological processes in zebrafish.
evidence: This is a claim about the broader applicability of the methods.

claim: The VAST BioImager can accommodate glass capillaries of 600–750 µm internal diameter, which allows imaging of zebrafish embryos and young larvae.
source: The VAST BioImager can accommodate glass capillaries of 600–750 µm internal diameter, which allows imaging of zebrafish embryos and young larvae (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This statement describes the technical specifications of the imaging system and references Figure 1C,D.

claim: All of the myelinating glial cells in a zebrafish larva at 4 days post fertilisation (dpf) could be imaged with a success rate of 83% in approximately 60 s using a 10X objective.
source: In initial tests using our transgenic reporter of myelinating oligodendrocytes, Tg(mbp:EGFP), we found that we could image all of the myelinating glial cells in a zebrafish larva at 4 days post fertilisation (dpf), with a success rate of 83%, in approximately 60 s, using a 10X objective (849 nm pixel size) (Figure 1E,F and Video 2).
evidence: This statement describes experimental results and references Figure 1E,F and Video 2.

claim: Manual counts of myelinating oligodendrocyte cells in 2D MIPs average 33.3 vs 3D stereological counts of 35.4.
source: Due to their sparse distribution, we found that myelinating oligodendrocyte number in the dorsal spinal cord could be reliably assessed by compressing 3D z-stacks into 2D maximum intensity projections (MIPs): manual counts of cells in 2D MIPs average 33.3 vs 3D stereological counts of 35.4 (Student's t-test, p=0.61, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement presents quantitative data and references Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is no statistically significant difference between manual counts of cells in 2D MIPs and 3D stereological counts (p=0.61).
source: Due to their sparse distribution, we found that myelinating oligodendrocyte number in the dorsal spinal cord could be reliably assessed by compressing 3D z-stacks into 2D maximum intensity projections (MIPs): manual counts of cells in 2D MIPs average 33.3 vs 3D stereological counts of 35.4 (Student's t-test, p=0.61, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement presents statistical analysis results.

claim: Following the fully automated ROI specification process in 196 animals, on average only 1.2 cells per animal were counted outwith the automatically assigned ROIs.
source: However, following the fully automated ROI specification process in 196 animals, we counted on average only 1.2 cells per animal outwith the automatically assigned ROIs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement presents quantitative data about the accuracy of the automated ROI specification and references Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: SKP2-C25 was identified as promoting myelination in a manual screen.
source: Following a manual screen to identify compounds that regulated myelination, using our Tg(mbp:EGFP-CAAX) reporter, we identified the compound SKP2-C25 as promoting myelination.
evidence: This statement describes a finding from a manual screen.

claim: Follow-up analyses showed that SKP2-C25 increased myelination, as assessed by electron microscopy, and did so by increasing oligodendrocyte number.
source: Follow-up analyses showed that SKP2-C25 increased myelination, as assessed by electron microscopy, and did so by increasing oligodendrocyte number (Almeida et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Almeida et al., 2018.

claim: SKP2-C25 is reported to be a selective inhibitor of the Skp2 SCF ubiquitin ligase complex that contributes to the ubiquitin-directed proteasomal degradation of proteins.
source: SKP2-C25 is reported to be a selective inhibitor of the Skp2 SCF ubiquitin ligase complex that contributes to the ubiquitin-directed proteasomal degradation of proteins (Chan et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Chan et al., 2013.

claim: Treatment of animals with SKP2-C25 increases the proliferation of OPCs between 2 and 3 dpf.
source: To exemplify the power of zebrafish to define how compounds affect specific stages of oligodendrocyte lineage progression, we show here, using time-lapse microscopy that treatment of animals with SKP2-C25 increases the proliferation of OPCs between 2 and 3 dpf (Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Video 6).
evidence: This statement presents experimental results and references Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Video 6.

claim: Oligodendrocytes differentiate by default in zebrafish to mediate the early myelination observed in the larval spinal cord.
source: We have previously shown that oligodendrocytes differentiate by default in zebrafish to mediate the early myelination observed in the larval spinal cord (Almeida et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Almeida et al., 2018.

claim: Upon an increase of OPC proliferation following SKP2-C25 treatment, there is a larger pool of OPCs that differentiate by default, leading to the observed increase in myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: Therefore, upon an increase of OPC proliferation following SKP2-C25 treatment, there is a larger pool of OPCs that differentiate by default, leading to the observed increase in myelinating oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed increase in OPC proliferation and the known default differentiation of oligodendrocytes.

claim: The imaging and analysis pipeline was able to detect increases in myelinating oligodendrocyte number following SKP2-C25 treatment.
source: We imaged control animals and those treated with a range of concentrations of SKP2-C25 using the VAST-SDCM, and found that our imaging and analysis pipeline was indeed able to detect increases in myelinating oligodendrocyte number (Figure 4).
evidence: This statement describes experimental validation of the imaging pipeline and references Figure 4.

claim: The study collated a small focused library of 175 compounds from three commercial sources (146 distinct molecular entities) that targeted enzymes implicated in epigenetic and post-translational modifications.
source: For this, we collated a small focused library of 175 compounds from three commercial sources (146 distinct molecular entities) that targeted enzymes implicated in epigenetic and post-translational modifications, given the known importance of epigenetic mechanisms during oligodendrocyte development (Copray et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the compound library used in the screen.

claim: Epigenetic mechanisms are important during oligodendrocyte development.
source: For this, we collated a small focused library of 175 compounds from three commercial sources (146 distinct molecular entities) that targeted enzymes implicated in epigenetic and post-translational modifications, given the known importance of epigenetic mechanisms during oligodendrocyte development (Copray et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Copray et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2016.

claim: The sample size needed to detect the increase in cell number seen for SKP2-C25 with 95% power and p<0.05 significance values was 9.
source: To ensure that our screen would detect relatively subtle changes in oligodendrocyte number, we calculated that the sample size needed to detect the increase in cell number seen for SKP2-C25 with 95% power and p<0.05 significance values was 9 (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This statement presents the results of a power calculation.

claim: 59/175 compounds were lethal at 100 µM.
source: We found that 59/175 compounds were lethal at 100 µM, 22/175 at 10 µM, and 0/175 at 1 µM.
evidence: This statement presents toxicity data from the screen.

claim: 22/175 compounds were lethal at 10 µM.
source: We found that 59/175 compounds were lethal at 100 µM, 22/175 at 10 µM, and 0/175 at 1 µM.
evidence: This statement presents toxicity data from the screen.

claim: 0/175 compounds were lethal at 1 µM.
source: We found that 59/175 compounds were lethal at 100 µM, 22/175 at 10 µM, and 0/175 at 1 µM.
evidence: This statement presents toxicity data from the screen.

claim: SKP2-C25 was effective in increasing oligodendrocyte number at 2 µM.
source: Given that SKP2-C25 was effective in increasing oligodendrocyte number at 2 µM, and the absence of any lethal compounds in our library at 1 µM, we decided to carry out our screen of myelinating oligodendrocyte number at 2 µM.
evidence: This statement describes the rationale for the screening concentration.

claim: Of the 146 unique compounds tested, 14 were identified as having a significant effect on oligodendrocyte number.
source: Of the 146 unique compounds tested, 14 were identified as having a significant effect on oligodendrocyte number.
evidence: This statement presents the primary screening results.

claim: Five compounds were identified as significantly increasing cell number, including the positive control SKP2-C25.
source: Statistical analysis of individual experiments (from single clutches) identified five compounds as significantly increasing cell number, including the positive control SKP2-C25, and nine as decreasing, all assessed by Ordinary one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc multiple comparisons test (see Materials and methods and Table 2).
evidence: This statement presents the screening results with statistical analysis.

claim: Nine compounds were identified as significantly decreasing oligodendrocyte cell number.
source: Statistical analysis of individual experiments (from single clutches) identified five compounds as significantly increasing cell number, including the positive control SKP2-C25, and nine as decreasing, all assessed by Ordinary one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc multiple comparisons test (see Materials and methods and Table 2).
evidence: This statement presents the screening results with statistical analysis.

claim: The positive control compound SKP2-C25 was included in two independent screening runs, but only returned as a statistically significant hit in one of those runs.
source: Our positive control compound was included in two independent screening runs, but only returned as a statistically significant hit in one of those runs.
evidence: This statement describes the variability in the positive control results.

claim: The screening run in which SKP2-C25 was not identified as a hit took twice as long to complete (8 vs 4 hr).
source: Interestingly, the screening run in which it was not identified as a hit took twice as long to complete (8 vs 4 hr), reflecting the fact that variability in cell numbers will increase with time, given ongoing development of live animals.
evidence: This statement presents data about screening duration and its effect on results.

claim: Two compounds (ML-228 and Trichostatin A) resulted in developmental lethality at the screening concentration used.
source: Two compounds (ML-228 and Trichostatin A) resulted in developmental lethality at the screening concentration used (Supplementary file 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement presents toxicity data from the screen.

claim: The automated and manually adjusted analyses revealed essentially identical effect sizes and identified the same hit compounds.
source: This comparison demonstrated that the automated and manually adjusted analyses revealed essentially identical effect sizes and identified the same hit compounds (Figure 5C and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This statement validates the automated analysis method and references Figure 5C and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Histone deacetylation plays a critical role in oligodendrocyte development.
source: In agreement with previous literature on the critical role of histone deacetylation for oligodendrocyte development (Cunliffe and Casaccia-Bonnefil, 2006; Liu et al., 2016), we found several HDAC (histone deacetylase) inhibitors in our set of 9 compounds that significantly reduced oligodendrocyte cell number (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D, Table 2 and Supplementary file 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Cunliffe and Casaccia-Bonnefil, 2006; Liu et al., 2016.

claim: Several HDAC (histone deacetylase) inhibitors significantly reduced oligodendrocyte cell number.
source: In agreement with previous literature on the critical role of histone deacetylation for oligodendrocyte development (Cunliffe and Casaccia-Bonnefil, 2006; Liu et al., 2016), we found several HDAC (histone deacetylase) inhibitors in our set of 9 compounds that significantly reduced oligodendrocyte cell number (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D, Table 2 and Supplementary file 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement presents screening results and references Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D, Table 2 and Supplementary files.

claim: Splitomicin demonstrated a 73% increase in MBP-expressing oligodendrocytes compared to controls (DMSO 41.7 ± 12.5 vs 2 μM splitomicin 72.3 ± 21.2, p=0.0001).
source: Of these, splitomicin, a sirtuin histone deacetylase inhibitor (Bedalov et al., 2001), and C646, a p300/CBP histone acetyltransferase inhibitor (Bowers et al., 2010), were the most effective in enhancing oligodendrocyte number, both demonstrating a 73% increase compared to controls (DMSO 41.7 ± 12.5 vs 2 μM splitomicin 72.3 ± 21.2 MBP +ve oligodendrocytes and DMSO 34.3 ± 10.1 vs 2 μM C646 59.1 ± 14.3; both p=0.0001; Supplementary file 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement presents quantitative data from the screen.

claim: C646 demonstrated a 73% increase in MBP-expressing oligodendrocytes compared to controls (DMSO 34.3 ± 10.1 vs 2 μM C646 59.1 ± 14.3, p=0.0001).

evidence: This statement presents quantitative data from the screen.

evidence: This statement presents quantitative data from the screen.

claim: NU9056 is a selective KAT5 (Tip60) histone acetyltransferase inhibitor.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Coffey et al., 2012.

evidence: This statement presents quantitative data from the screen.

claim: All four hit compounds were lethal at 10 and 20 µM.
source: All four compounds were lethal at 10 and 20 µM.
evidence: This statement presents toxicity data from concentration series analyses.

claim: NU9056 re-treatment did not demonstrate an increase in cell number at any concentration.
source: NU9056 re-treatment did not demonstrate an increase in cell number at any concentration (Figure 6), suggesting the possibility that its identification in our screen represented a false positive.
evidence: This statement presents data from follow-up experiments and references Figure 6.

claim: Splitomicin, C646 and GSK-J5 recapitulated the observed increases in oligodendrocyte number identified in the screen.
source: However, splitomicin, C646 and GSK-J5 recapitulated the observed increases in oligodendrocyte number identified in the screen (Figure 6).
evidence: This statement presents validation data and references Figure 6.

claim: The region representing the second of five tiles along the length of the spinal cord was the most sensitive to changes in myelinating oligodendrocyte number.
source: Our region-specific assessment of hit compounds indicated that the region representing the second of five tiles along the length of the spinal cord was the most sensitive to changes in myelinating oligodendrocyte number, wherein all five compounds had significant increases in myelinating oligodendrocyte number (Figure 7E and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This statement presents data from region-specific analyses and references Figure 7E and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Analyses in single tile mode would be sufficient to detect hit compounds regulating cell number for future screens.
source: These data suggest that analyses in single tile mode would be sufficient to detect hit compounds regulating cell number for future screens.
evidence: This is an inference based on the region-specific analysis results.

claim: Imaging one instead of 5-tiled z-stacks per animal would more than double the throughput of future screens, allowing assessment of myelinating oligodendrocyte number in 85 animals per hour, instead of 40 per hour.
source: Imaging one instead of 5-tiled z-stacks per animal would more than double the throughput of future screens, and allow us to assess myelinating oligodendrocyte number in 85 animals per hour, instead of the initial screen throughput of 40 per hour (Table 1).
evidence: This statement presents a calculation about screening throughput and references Table 1.

claim: Automated quantification of splitomicin-treated larvae revealed a significant increase in mean dorsal fluorescence intensity over multiple concentrations compared with control-treated larvae.
source: Automated quantification of splitomicin-treated larvae revealed a significant increase in mean dorsal fluorescence intensity over multiple concentrations compared with control-treated larvae, despite this being difficult to subjectively appreciate by eye (average dorsal grey values – 3 × 3 binning 60 ms exposure, DMSO 136.1 ± 35.9 vs 2 μM splitomicin 174.7 ± 34.3, p=0.0023; 3 μM splitomicin 186.4 ± 33.3, p=0.0001; 4 μM splitomicin 203.4 ± 38.3, p=0.0001 Figure 8B).
evidence: This statement presents quantitative data from fluorescence intensity analysis and references Figure 8B.

claim: Transmission electron microscopy on 4 dpf larvae found a ~1.8 fold increase in myelinated axon number in splitomicin-treated animals (DMSO 9.8 ± 4.3 vs 2 μM splitomicin 18 ± 2.6, p=0.0065).
source: To confirm that this increase in fluorescence did indeed reflect a change in bona fide myelination, we performed transmission electron microscopy on 4 dpf larvae and found a ~1.8 fold increase in myelinated axon number in splitomicin-treated animals (DMSO 9.8 ± 4.3 vs 2 μM splitomicin 18 ± 2.6, p=0.0065; Figure 8C–E).
evidence: This statement presents quantitative data from electron microscopy and references Figure 8C–E.

claim: Treatment of rat primary oligodendrocytes with splitomicin resulted in a robust increase in the number of MBP expressing oligodendrocytes.
source: Finally, to test whether compound function in zebrafish was conserved in mammals, we tested whether treatment of rat primary oligodendrocytes with splitomicin also affected the mammalian oligodendrocyte lineage. Indeed, we found that two-day treatment of cultures immediately following plate-down (see Materials and methods) resulted in a robust increase in the number of MBP expressing oligodendrocytes (Figure 9).
evidence: This statement presents data from mammalian cell culture experiments and references Figure 9.

claim: Splitomicin treatment increased the number of Ki67-expressing, olig2-expressing cells in rat primary oligodendrocyte cultures.
source: Furthermore, we assessed proliferation (using an antibody recognising Ki67) of oligodendrocyte lineage cells (using an antibody recognising olig2). We saw an increase in the number of Ki67-expressing, olig2-expressing cells, upon splitomicin treatment (Figure 9), indicating that the observed increase in myelinating oligodendrocyte number was due to increased proliferation and subsequent differentiation of a larger pool of OPCs.
evidence: This statement presents data from mammalian cell culture experiments and references Figure 9.

claim: The observed increase in myelinating oligodendrocyte number in rat cultures was due to increased proliferation and subsequent differentiation of a larger pool of OPCs.
source: Furthermore, we assessed proliferation (using an antibody recognising Ki67) of oligodendrocyte lineage cells (using an antibody recognising olig2). We saw an increase in the number of Ki67-expressing, olig2-expressing cells, upon splitomicin treatment (Figure 9), indicating that the observed increase in myelinating oligodendrocyte number was due to increased proliferation and subsequent differentiation of a larger pool of OPCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed increase in Ki67+ olig2+ cells.

claim: The identification of splitomicin as a regulator of the oligodendrocyte lineage in zebrafish was validated as having the capacity to regulate the mammalian oligodendrocyte lineage.
source: Therefore, our identification of splitomicin as a regulator of the oligodendrocyte lineage in zebrafish was validated as having the capacity to regulate the mammalian oligodendrocyte lineage.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mammalian cell culture experiments.

claim: The VAST-SDCM platform can image all of the myelinating glial cells in a zebrafish larva at 4 dpf in approximately 60 s using a 10X objective with 849 nm pixel size.
source: In initial tests using our transgenic reporter of myelinating oligodendrocytes, Tg(mbp:EGFP), we found that we could image all of the myelinating glial cells in a zebrafish larva at 4 days post fertilisation (dpf), with a success rate of 83%, in approximately 60 s, using a 10X objective (849 nm pixel size) (Figure 1E,F and Video 2).
evidence: This statement presents technical performance data and references Figure 1E,F and Video 2.

claim: The VAST-SDCM platform achieved an 83% success rate in imaging zebrafish larvae.
source: In initial tests using our transgenic reporter of myelinating oligodendrocytes, Tg(mbp:EGFP), we found that we could image all of the myelinating glial cells in a zebrafish larva at 4 days post fertilisation (dpf), with a success rate of 83%, in approximately 60 s, using a 10X objective (849 nm pixel size) (Figure 1E,F and Video 2).
evidence: This statement presents technical performance data.

claim: The VAST BioImager capillary can be rotated fully (360 degrees) around the x-axis.
source: The capillary can be rotated fully (360 degrees) around the x-axis (Figure 1C,D; Video 1), such that animals can be automatically oriented according to user-defined templates (Pardo-Martin et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement describes a technical feature of the system and references Figure 1C,D and Video 1.

claim: Animals can be automatically oriented according to user-defined templates using the VAST BioImager.

evidence: This statement describes a technical feature and is supported by a citation to Pardo-Martin et al., 2010.

claim: The completely automated process can process an individual sample in under a second and 288 animals in a 96 well plate in 3.5 min.
source: For example, the completely automated process can process an individual sample in under a second and the 288 animals in a 96 well plate in 3.5 min.
evidence: This statement presents performance data for the automated analysis.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Bedalov et al., 2001.

claim: Splitomicin has reported activity for sirtuin 1 and 2 (sirt1 and sirt2) in mammalian cells in vitro.
source: Splitomicin is a small molecule inhibitor of the sirtuin family of NAD+-dependent HDACs (Bedalov et al., 2001), with reported activity for sirtuin 1 and 2 (sirt1 and sirt2) in mammalian cells in vitro (Pasco et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pasco et al., 2010.

claim: Sirt1 shows broad protein expression throughout the rodent CNS.
source: Sirt1 shows broad protein expression throughout the rodent CNS (Sidorova-Darmos et al., 2014), but has been implicated in regulating the oligodendrocyte lineage.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sidorova-Darmos et al., 2014.

claim: Conditional genetic inactivation of sirt1 in adult rodent neural stem cells led to an increase in OPC formation, and a consequent increase in remyelination following toxin-induced demyelination.
source: For example, conditional genetic inactivation of sirt1 in adult rodent neural stem cells led to an increase in OPC formation, and a consequent increase in remyelination following toxin-induced demyelination (Rafalski et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Rafalski et al., 2013.

claim: The opposite effect on the oligodendrocyte lineage has been reported in neonatal animals, with reduced numbers of proliferating OPCs following sirt1 knockdown and increased oligodendrocyte differentiation under hypoxic conditions.
source: Interestingly, the opposite effect on the oligodendrocyte lineage has been reported in neonatal animals, with reduced numbers of proliferating OPCs following sirt1 knockdown and increased oligodendrocyte differentiation under hypoxic conditions suggesting a context-dependent role for sirt1 (Jablonska et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Jablonska et al., 2016.

claim: Sirt2 expression is highly enriched in the oligodendrocyte lineage, and is upregulated in newly differentiating and myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: In contrast to sirt1, sirt2 expression is highly enriched in the oligodendrocyte lineage, and is upregulated in newly differentiating and myelinating oligodendrocytes (Werner et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Werner et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2014.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Bowers et al., 2010.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Nakashima et al., 1999; Zhang et al., 2016.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Dai et al., 2015.

claim: GSK-J5 is recommended as a structure-matched inactive control for the more active isomer, GSK-J4.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kruidenier et al., 2012.

claim: GSK-J4 and other selective JMJ inhibitors within the library had no effect on oligodendrocyte number in the screen.
source: This fact, coupled with the finding that GSK-J4 and other selective JMJ inhibitors within the library had no effect on oligodendrocyte number in our screen, suggests that GSK-J5 may promote myelinating oligodendrocyte formation through an alternative target, again highlighting the issue of target validation (Schenone et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement presents data from the screen.

claim: GSK-J5 may promote myelinating oligodendrocyte formation through an alternative target.
source: This fact, coupled with the finding that GSK-J4 and other selective JMJ inhibitors within the library had no effect on oligodendrocyte number in our screen, suggests that GSK-J5 may promote myelinating oligodendrocyte formation through an alternative target, again highlighting the issue of target validation (Schenone et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the screening results.

claim: Most compounds are likely to bind to more than one target in vivo.
source: Given that most compounds are likely to bind to more than one target in vivo, if several compounds with an overlapping target elicit the same phenotype, then one has a better foundation upon which to pursue the more challenging genetic and biochemical methods of target validation.
evidence: This is a general statement about compound specificity.

claim: The VAST-SDCM system has multiple excitation laser lines and two cameras that allow simultaneous imaging in two channels without any increase in imaging time.
source: The system has multiple excitation laser lines and two cameras that allow simultaneous imaging in two channels without any increase in imaging time, meaning that two assays could be screened in parallel, given appropriate reporters, or several reporters in parallel with some increase in imaging times.
evidence: This statement describes the technical capabilities of the system.

claim: The platform can accommodate photo-ablation and photo-activation lasers for acute manipulations.
source: In addition, the platform can accommodate photo-ablation and photo-activation lasers for acute manipulations, and the stability of larvae in the imaging capillary, and speed of the SDCM imaging system is such that up to minutes long time-lapse microscopy could, in principle, be carried out on individual animals.
evidence: This statement describes the technical capabilities of the system.

claim: A recent update to the liquid handling system means that the platform can be configured such that zebrafish can be dispensed back in to the wells of multi-well plates from the BioImager.
source: A recent update to the liquid handling system now means that the platform can be configured such that zebrafish can be dispensed back in to the wells of multi-well plates from the BioImager, allowing for collection of embryos for further study, for example genotyping or re-imaging.
evidence: This statement describes a technical update to the system.
